title: Lights Out
placeholderNote: Kordav, Elsin and Marrat are fictional countries. All officials, companies, crews and agencies are fictional.
frozenText: The minister has taken the recovery out of her hands. Nothing you brief today changes what is done to the grid.

briefing.dateLine: The 9th. January, in the first hard cold of the winter.
situation: At 0312 this morning the control systems for Elsin's northern power grid, and for the pumping controls on the Southern Line, were encrypted. A criminal crew called Grey Ledger has claimed the attack and wants paying. Kalsa is on rolling blackouts.
Your cell has been lent to the alliance's Infrastructure Protection Cell in Kalsa for as long as this lasts. Its director is Ilse Brandt, an engineer.

She has three ways to get the lights back. Pay the ransom and use the crew's decryptor: a day, if the crew wants it to work. Restore the six control servers from the vendor's clean images: two days, trusting what the vendor's update server sends. Rebuild them by hand from parts and paper: nine more days of blackouts in January.

The lab's findings, the grid operator, the vendor, the crew's own messages and public reporting reach you every day. Everything else has to be tasked. Liaison requests go to Kalsa's ministries over LATTICE.

customer.name: Director Ilse Brandt
customer.wants: Who did this, so she knows which way to fix it?
customer.context: She has no patience for estimative language and says so. And the minister has a clock of his own.
customer.tipLine: She only moves on High. Medium and Low get nothing done.

opening.text: I've read your file. I need a name, and a level of certainty I can act on. I act on one level only.
opening.reassigned: They've sent me a new cell. The grid doesn't care who you were. Who did this?

byLastTone.good: Your file says you get it right. I need it right, and in one word. Who?

policySummary.action: Orders a rebuild by hand, and tells the operators to trust nothing supplied from outside
Orders a restore from the vendor's images, and recommends Elsin expel Marrat's remaining advisers
Nothing. "I can't run a grid on a maybe."

policyNote: She only moves on High. If she has ordered nothing by 1800 on the 13th, the minister's restore goes ahead.

replyLabels.restore: Orders a restore from the vendor's images
replyLabels.frozen: Can't decide the recovery: the minister has taken it

replies.paid: Paid. If the decryptor works, we're back by tomorrow night. If it doesn't, that is on me.
replies.rebuild: Rebuild by hand, starting now. Nothing from outside touches those servers. Nine days. The minister is not pleased.
replies.restore: Vendor restore ordered. I've also told the minister which advisers he should send home.
replies.stands: Already ordered. Tell me if anything changes.
replies.maybe: That's a maybe. I can't run a grid on a maybe.
replies.frozen: The decision is the minister's now. Bring me something I can put in front of him.
replies.overruled: Six hours in, on your call, I told the minister it was Kordav. He asked what we had. I said: an assessment. He has taken the recovery out of my hands, and says he will take advice from people with evidence.
replies.decryptor: The decryptor works on the office machines. On all six control servers it fails, and leaves them in a worse state than before. We paid for the part that didn't matter.

events.note: Nothing you brief for three days changes what is done to the grid. Your last brief will.
The money is gone and the control servers are still dark. She is back where she started.

hypotheses.text: Grey Ledger did this for money, as it has nineteen times before.
hypotheses.claim: Grey Ledger did this for money

hypotheses.text: Kordav is behind it, using the crew as cover.
hypotheses.claim: Kordav is behind it, using the crew as cover

hypotheses.text: Marrat is behind it, still sore about the pipeline.

groundTruth.state: Grey Ledger, paid 1.1 million in advance by a Bureau front, encrypted the six control servers it was told to hit. The ransom demand is real: the crew would like to be paid twice.

groundTruth.bestCall: H2 at Medium (High with the wallet or PETREL)
groundTruth.state: The lab finds the Marrat-language strings the Bureau had appended. The crew, told to keep the victim talking, cuts its price without being asked.
The minister sets his deadline, which is the one the Bureau was counting on.
The Bureau posts a forged chat log blaming "the liaison office." The altered images sit ready on Corvane's update server, built two days before the attack.
Kordav's broadcaster amplifies the forgery. At 1800 the images go in unless someone stops them.

adversaryPlan.phase: A criminal face, then a Marrat accent
adversaryPlan.summary: Break six servers, and let the vendor and the minister do the rest.
Point at a person, and keep everyone busy until 1800 on the 13th.

sources.access: The Infrastructure Protection Cell's forensic team. Careful, and slower than anyone would like.
sources.postmortemNote: Reported what it found, including the appended strings, and said they were appended.

sources.access: Elsin's grid operator and the energy minister's office
sources.postmortemNote: The minister and Lind meant well. Lind's memo was true.

sources.access: Corvane Systems, which built and maintains the control servers. Honest about what it knows.
sources.postmortemNote: Honest. It didn't know what its update server was holding.

sources.access: Elsin's military intelligence liaison desk, Col. E. Rhun
sources.postmortemNote: Right about the wallet. Her paper copy never left her safe.

sources.access: Grey Ledger's own posts and ransom messages
sources.postmortemNote: Hired. The crew told the truth as it understood it. It didn't know who the client was.

sources.access: A broker on criminal forums who has dealt with Grey Ledger. He hears what the crew complains about. New. Don't task him two days running.
sources.postmortemNote: He heard the crew complain, which was exactly what was needed.
A state outlet, telling the truth: Marrat really didn't do it.

reports.text:
Grid operator: at 0312 the six control servers for the northern grid and the Southern Line's pumping controls were encrypted. Both are now being run by hand. The operator's office network is also down.
Blackouts are scheduled district by district.
reports.postmortemNote: What was hit: six control servers, and only incidentally the office network.

reports.text: Ransom message from Grey Ledger: 4 million in cryptocurrency within 96 hours. "Nothing personal. Pay, receive the decryptor, and we never meet again. Ask our previous customers."
reports.postmortemNote: A real crew making a real demand. True, and not the story.

reports.text:
Lab finding, first pass.
Malware: a known Grey Ledger strain.
Entry: a contractor's remote-access account.
Behaviour: it went straight to the six control servers by name, and ignored some four hundred other machines until those six were done.
reports.postmortemNote: The item that made Low on Kordav defensible. Criminals take everything. Somebody chose these six.

reports.text: From Corvane: we can supply clean system images for all six control servers from our update server within 24 hours of a request. Standard recovery is two days to full operation.
reports.postmortemNote: An honest offer. It was also the trap, stated on Day 1 by a man who didn't know.

reports.text: Cell admin: our own building has power. It does not have heating. Facilities describe these as separate systems.
reports.postmortemNote: Heating.

reports.text:
Lab finding.
The malware's loader contains text strings in Marrat's language, and its build times fall within office hours in Marrat.
The strings sit in a section appended after the program was built.
reports.postmortemNote: A false trail, accurately reported by an honest lab.

reveal.tell: The lab says it in the item: the strings sit in a section appended after the program was built.

crossCheck.text: The strain is Grey Ledger's own, used nineteen times before (R-1-02, R-1-03), and none of those carried Marrat's language. For one point, the language check (C-08) shows the strings are machine-translated.

reveal.motive: Marrat had a motive everyone remembered from the pipeline. If the criminal story failed, the next suspect was ready.

reports.text: Marrat News Agency: Marrat's government "categorically denies any involvement," and offers to send engineers to help Elsin recover.
reports.postmortemNote: A true denial. A denial tells you nothing either way.

reports.text: Grey Ledger posts a sample of stolen office documents as proof. Unasked, it lowers its demand to 2.5 million "for a quick close."
reports.postmortemNote: A crew discounting unasked on day two. It had been told not to close.

reports.text: Kalsa: Elsin's energy minister says "all options are open," and that he expects power restored "within days, not weeks."
reports.postmortemNote: The political clock starts.

reports.text: Cell admin: portable heaters have been issued. They may not be plugged in during a scheduled blackout, which is when they are needed.
reports.postmortemNote: Heaters.

reports.text: From the minister's office: restoration from the vendor's images will begin at 1800 on the 13th, unless Director Brandt gives the minister a reason, in writing, to do something else.
reports.postmortemNote: The default. If you gave Brandt nothing, this happened.

reports.text:
Lab finding.
The remote-access account belongs to a Corvane field engineer. His credentials were valid. He says he was asleep.
The malware carried a list of six server names that matches the as-built network diagram, issue 7.
Issue 7 went to five named holders on paper three weeks ago. One electronic copy was lodged with the alliance over LATTICE.
reports.postmortemNote: The map: issue 7, five paper copies and one electronic copy.

reports.text:
Col. Rhun, liaison desk: "My service has traced part of the ransom wallet's history. Grey Ledger received 1.1 million two weeks before the attack, from an exchange in Kordav's capital. Criminals are not usually paid in advance."
Sourcing: her service's own tracing.
reports.postmortemNote: Rhun, right again, with the fact that settled who was paying. The same fact was available a day earlier for one point.

reports.text: Kordav's state broadcaster leads with Kalsa in the dark: "An alliance that cannot keep its friends warm."
reports.postmortemNote: Gloating. Kordav was enjoying this, which it would have either way.

reports.text: Cell admin: the heaters have been recalled. One of them was plugged in.
reports.postmortemNote: Heaters.

reports.text:
An anonymous post on a criminal forum claims to be a leaked Grey Ledger chat log. In it the negotiator writes: "We are obliged to our esteemed friend in the liaison office in Kalsa, who provided the diagram."
Unverified.
reports.postmortemNote: A forgery, aimed at a person.

reveal.tell: The voice. Grey Ledger writes "Nothing personal. Pay, receive the decryptor, and we never meet again." This log says "We are obliged to our esteemed friend." It reads like a civil servant's idea of a criminal.

crossCheck.text: The liaison desk held a paper copy of the diagram (R-3-02). For two points, the lab's comparison (C-06) shows the attackers' list was copied from the electronic one.

reveal.motive: To start a hunt for a traitor in an office, so that nobody looked anywhere else.

reports.text: Grey Ledger extends its own deadline by a day and lowers the demand to 1.5 million. "We are reasonable people."
reports.postmortemNote: Lower again, later again. A crew that didn't want to finish.

reports.text: From Corvane: the images are staged on our update server and our engineer is on site. We can have the first control server running six hours after the order.
reports.postmortemNote: Ready and waiting, and honestly offered.

reports.text: Deputy Director O. Lind, in a memo to the minister, copied to Brandt: "A rebuild by hand means nine more days of blackouts in January. People will die of it. I recommend the vendor restore."
reports.postmortemNote: The hardest true item in the scenario. Lind was right about the cost and wrong about the choice, and he isn't a villain.

reports.text: Cell admin: staff are reminded that the building's fire alarm also depends on mains power.
reports.postmortemNote: The fire alarm.

reports.text: Grid operator: restoration from Corvane's images begins at 1800. Corvane's engineer is in the control room.
reports.postmortemNote: The deadline.

reports.text:
Kordav's state broadcaster: "Elsin hunts a traitor in its own liaison office as the capital freezes."
It first ran the line four hours after the forum post appeared.
reports.postmortemNote: The forgery, made respectable.

reveal.tell: State television led with a detail from an anonymous forum post within four hours of it appearing.

crossCheck.text: One origin (R-4-01), repeated by the broadcaster of the state that wrote it.

reveal.motive: To make the forgery respectable enough to act on.

reports.text: Col. Rhun, liaison desk: "I know what is being said about my desk. My copy of issue 7 has been in my safe since the day it was handed to me. You are welcome to come and look."
reports.postmortemNote: True. Her copy was in her safe. She was angry, and entitled to be.

reports.text:
Lab finding.
Corvane's update server holds a new image set for this model of control server, dated the 7th: two days before the attack.
Corvane's published schedule shows no release this winter.
reports.postmortemNote: The best evidence that arrived unasked: the cure was prepared two days before the disease.

reports.text: Cell admin: heating has been restored to the building. Power is now intermittent.
reports.postmortemNote: Heating.

reports.text: Chain analysis of the wallet named in the ransom note: it received 1.1 million two weeks before the attack, in one payment, from an exchange in Kordav's capital. Nothing else came in until this week.
reports.postmortemNote: Paid in advance, from Kordav's capital. One point, and it justified High on Day 2.

reports.text:
Source reports: Grey Ledger took a contract last month. "Hit six boxes, leave the rest, paid up front." The crew thinks the client is another gang. They were told which six.
Access: what crew members have told him.
reports.postmortemNote: A contract job: six boxes, paid up front, told which six.

reports.text:
Source reports: the crew is fed up. The client has told them to keep talking and not to close. "The money doesn't matter. Keep them busy until the 13th."
Access: what crew members have told him.
reports.postmortemNote: The client knew the minister's deadline.

reports.text:
The negotiator's communications: his instructions arrive through a relay that also carries traffic for a trading company in Kordav's capital.
Comment: that company has fronted for the Bureau before.
reports.postmortemNote: The handler's relay.

reports.text: Marrat's energy ministry: officials are alarmed that their language is being found in the malware. The minister has ordered an inquiry of his own, and has asked who is trying to embarrass him.
reports.postmortemNote: Clears Marrat. They were as surprised as anyone.

reports.text:
Lab comparison of the target list with the diagram.
The malware's list spells one server "PCS-O6", with a letter O.
The five paper copies of issue 7 print "PCS-06", with a zero.
The electronic copy lodged over LATTICE has the letter O.
reports.postmortemNote: The letter O. The attackers' map was the electronic copy.

reports.text:
In answer to our request, Kalsa's registry lists five paper copies of issue 7: Director Brandt; Deputy Director O. Lind; Col. E. Rhun, liaison desk; Maj. T. Arle, Task Force VEYL; and Corvane's site engineer.
Maj. Arle's copy was never collected. He has been on leave, and it is still sealed in the registry.
One electronic copy was lodged over LATTICE.
reports.postmortemNote: The five names, and a copy that was never collected.

reports.text: Kordav's state broadcaster, in passing: "Officials in Kalsa spent yesterday searching their own registry for who holds which documents."
reports.postmortemNote: Your request to the registry, on Kordav's television the next day.

reports.text: Language check on the Marrat strings: two errors typical of machine translation, and one word that Marrat's speakers stopped using decades ago.
reports.postmortemNote: The strings were machine-translated.

reports.text: Corvane's public release log shows no update for this model of control server since the spring. Its update server nonetheless lists a new image set dated the 7th.
reports.postmortemNote: An unscheduled image set dated two days before the attack. One point, from Day 1.

reports.text:
Lab examination of the staged images.
Built on the 7th by an automated job that nobody at Corvane scheduled.
They include a remote-management component that isn't on Corvane's published build list.
reports.postmortemNote: Something in the images that isn't on the build list.

tellLabels.out-of-register: Not in the source's own voice
tellLabels.too-on-message: Says exactly what someone needs said

endings.title: Clean
endings.text: The control servers are rebuilt from parts and paper. Power comes back district by district over nine days. Nobody thanks Brandt in January. In March the lab finishes with Corvane's images, and the minister asks to see her.

endings.title: Clean, and cold
endings.text: The control servers are rebuilt from parts and paper, starting late. The blackouts run into a third week. In March the lab finishes with Corvane's images, and the minister asks to see Brandt.

endings.title: Lights on
endings.text: Corvane's images go in at 1800 on the 13th. Power is back in two days. The minister is photographed in a control room.

dailyUpdates.text: Kalsa is on rolling blackouts. Grey Ledger has claimed the attack.
A second night of blackouts. The main hospital is on generators.
The energy minister has set a deadline.
Corvane's images are ready. The minister's deadline is tomorrow evening.
The vendor restore begins at 1800 today unless Brandt countermands it.

script.text: A real crew made a real demand. The malware passed four hundred machines to reach six. The vendor offered clean images, in good faith.
The lab found Marrat's language in the malware, and reported that it had been added after the build. The crew cut its price without being asked.
The minister set a deadline. Rhun reported that the crew had been paid in advance, from Kordav's capital.
A chat log appeared in a voice the crew had never used, thanking a friend in the liaison office. Brandt's deputy wrote that a rebuild would cost lives. About the cold, he was right.
Kordav's broadcaster had put the forgery in a headline within four hours. The images that were supposed to fix everything had been built two days before anything broke.

lessons: Ask what the attacker needs you to do next. The damage here was a means. The aim was the repair.
A crew that keeps lowering its price isn't working for the ransom. Grey Ledger had already been paid.
Compare an item's voice with its supposed author. The chat log read like nothing Grey Ledger had ever sent.
A true cost can sit beside a wrong choice. Lind was right about nine days of cold, and wrong about the restore.
Know what your customer can act on. Brandt could use High, and nothing else.

missedCollection.1: The ransom wallet's history (OSINT, one point): the crew was paid in advance from Kordav's capital.
missedCollection.2: The lab's comparison of the target list with the diagram, or PETREL.
missedCollection.3: The negotiator's communications (SIGINT): his instructions come through a Bureau front.
missedCollection.4: The lab's examination of Corvane's images: they hold something that isn't on the build list.
missedCollection.5: Nothing tasked today could arrive in time.

postmortem.openQuestion: The attackers' list spelled one server the way only the electronic copy of the diagram spells it. And if you asked Kalsa's registry who held the diagram, Kordav's broadcaster mentioned the search the next day.

pirs.question: Who is Grey Ledger working for this time?
How did the malware know where to go?

targets.name: Compare the malware's target list with the network diagram
Ask the registry who holds the diagram
targets.fallback: The registry has nothing to add.

collection.note: Liaison requests go to Kalsa's ministries over LATTICE.

burnRules.postmortem: PETREL was tasked two days running. A broker who asks about the same crew twice in two days gets noticed.

levels.label: Questioned
levels.text: Her office trims your collection: 1 point less a day.

levels.label: Discounted
levels.text: 2 points less a day. She still acts on a High: she has nothing else to act on.

triggers.rule: The minister overrules her for acting on your word
triggers.note: Credibility −2. She put a judgment in front of a minister who wanted evidence.

triggers.rule: Money she paid on your word buys nothing
triggers.note: Credibility −1. She paid on your word, and it bought nothing.

triggers.rule: Three days running without a High (each further day too)
triggers.note: Credibility −1. Three days without a High. "I asked for one word."

credibility.summary: Brandt is new to you, so she starts from your file. She can't see whether you're right. She can see money wasted, a minister overruling her, and days going by without an answer she can use.

caseFile.text: You kept the vendor's images off the grid's control servers.
You had the lab compare the target list with the diagram. The attackers' map was the electronic copy, not one of the five on paper.
You asked Kalsa's registry who held the diagram, and Kordav's broadcaster mentioned the search the next day.
You doubted the chat log that pointed at the liaison office.

analysts.name: Imre Vasko
analysts.reveal: He settles on a reading early. It was Marrat on Day 1, and the planted strings seemed to confirm it on Day 2. By Day 4 he had moved on to a person. He was sincere each time, and wrong each time.

analysts.name: Noor Halden
analysts.reveal: Careful, and slow. She wasn't wrong once. Each of her notes pointed at something you could have tasked the day before.

analysts.name: Tess Marrow
analysts.reveal: Quick, and sure of herself. Wrong that it was about money. After that: half right about the discount, properly careful about wallet tracing from a liaison service, and sharp about the broadcaster. Her best scenario so far.

notes.text: Grey Ledger: nineteen victims in three years, always for money, always pay and walk away. It's them, and it's about money.
notes.why: It was them. It wasn't about money.

notes.text: Marrat lost a pact over that pipeline, and now the pumps are dark. I'd look at who gains.
notes.why: Marrat was as surprised as anyone.

notes.text: Marrat's language in the code. That is what I expected.
They never discount this early. That's odd. Maybe they need the cash.
notes.why: Odd, yes. They didn't need the cash.

notes.text: Four hundred machines to choose from, and it went straight to six. That isn't scanning. Something told it where to go.
Wallet tracing from a liaison service? I'd want to see the chain data myself.
notes.why: The right instinct, and the chain data was there for one point.

notes.text: The lab says the strings were appended after the build. A programmer's own language runs all through the code. It doesn't arrive in one block at the end.
The liaison office. That's Rhun's desk. She has had it in for half of Kalsa for years.
notes.why: He took a forgery at its word.

notes.text: Six names on a target list. I'd like to see how each one is spelled, next to the diagram.
State TV had "liaison office" in a headline four hours after an anonymous forum post. That's quick, even for them.
Before anyone installs an image, I'd want to know when it was built and who asked for it.
